text:
maria: quick probe — running a small recon job for tenant credits and saw a weird pattern: some tenants temporarily show +2 credits for the same ingest id during compaction window. sample attached.

sam: ugh. is that in the compacted ledger or only the fast-path live view?

maria: compacted ledger. fast-path looked fine. suspect race between compact job and the ingest ACK path that marks residency. Could be a window where both pre-compact and post-compact traces are credited.

alex: do we have an example id? can you paste the minimal event chain? helps to reason about ordering.

maria: here — simplified chain:
```
INGEST: event{id: E1, tenant: T42, tokens: 10} -> write to raw
COMPACT START: picks raw batch including E1
ACK PATH: ingest marks claim for T42 on shard S1
COMPACT MERGE: produces compact record with net 20 (duplicate merge)
```
appears compact merged a duplicate from a retry that ingest already accepted, so compact ended up summing instead of deduping.

jia: is dedupe key the event id or fingerprint? we changed fingerprinting earlier to use prefix+hash which may differ across retry attempts.

maria: exactly. retry produced a slightly different fingerprint because metadata order changed, so compact didn't correlate.

denise: two separate problems: (1) dedupe identity fragility and (2) residency/claim timing — the ingest ACK might be writing a _claim_ record that later gets compacted away, and compact then replays tokens into the ledger.

sam: i'd treat (1) as correctness (stable fingerprint) and (2) as an invariant: compact must never add tokens that have been accounted by a confirmed claim. We need a contract between ingest and compactor.

alex: propose contract: ingest writes claim records with idempotency token = canonical_event_id. compactor uses canonical_event_id (if present) as dedupe key; if absent, treat record as provisional and require a reconciliation phase.

maria: leaning that way. but how expensive is it to require canonical ids for all ingesters? some SDKs still emit only payload hashes.

jia: we can add a best-effort canonicalizer in ingest path: if canonical_event_id missing, compute normalized hash (stable sort keys, strip noisy metadata). document corner cases.

denise: fallback: compactor should consult a small lease index before applying net-adds. Pattern:
- compactor computes delta
- compactor checks claim index (recent window) for canonical_event_id or matching fingerprint
- if claim present, skip applying delta; else apply and emit audit flag
This keeps compactor defensive for late-claim races.

sam: that lease check adds an extra read per batch; can be cached/readonly and window-limited to reduce cost. Acceptable if turned on for rolling migration only.

maria: sounds good. also: auditing — when compactor skips due to claim, emit an audit event with reasoning so billing can prove non-duplication. ops-bot: would love a retriable log here.

ops-bot: audit-event created: audit_id=AU_5291234567, severity=INFO, note="compactor-skip-due-to-claim"

alex: we also need to avoid unbounded claim index growth. keep TTL ~48h and rely on finalizer to reconcile older tails. For very late arrivals, run a backfill job.

jia: one more thought: compact should not reingest token totals blindly — apply a subtract-then-add framed by event-level dedupe. Pseudocode:
```
for batch in compact_batches:
  for event in batch:
    key = event.canonical_id or fingerprint(event)
    if seen_in_claim_index(key): continue
    delta = compute_delta(event)
    ledger.apply_atomic_delta(account=tenant, delta)
```
```
This avoids summing duplicates.

denise: agree. and surface a metric: compactor.skips_due_to_claim and compactor.applied_conflicts. We'll need an alert threshold to catch regressions.

maria: action items:
- [alex] design claim index TTL and storage (Dynamo/kv) + caching layer — due EOW
- [jia] add canonicalizer shim to ingest path with tests — 2w
- [sam] prototype compactor lease-check + audit emission, toggle via feature flag — 1w
- [denise] add metrics and alert spec — PR by next Wed

sam: also propose a small reconcile job run nightly for any compacted deltas with audit flags — easier to debug customer disputes.

maria: +1. will file a follow-up RFC for the ingest/compactor contract and include sample events and metrics. tagging @alex @jia to review.

alex: will review. can we include a minimal e2e test in CI that injects retries with metadata reordering to prevent regressions? :thumbsup:

maria: yes — e2e test included in RFC checklist. thanks all.
__note: This thread contains short, conversational Slack-style messages. Field names limited to simple strings and lists per agents.md.
